title: C Y P two D six and codeine

segs.text: Section ten. C Y P two D six, debrisoquine, and codeine. C Y P two D six was the first P four fifty enzyme studied in depth, and it is the best characterized. She said, It metabolizes about fifteen to twenty five percent of the medications on the market, so that's a lot of work that it does.

Debrisoquine is cleared almost entirely by C Y P two D six. So when people are grouped by the ratio of parent drug to metabolite, the trait is monogenic, meaning one gene drives it. The data separate into distinct peaks for ultrarapid, extensive, and poor metabolizers. A smooth bell curve would mean the opposite, that many genes blur the data together.

Each phenotype has a genotype behind it. Extra copies of the whole gene, written star two times N, make an ultrarapid metabolizer with very fast clearance or activation. Two wild type copies make an extensive, or normal, metabolizer, which is the common middle of the distribution. Star five over star five is a whole gene deletion, not an ultrarapid allele, so no enzyme is expressed and the person is a poor metabolizer.

More than one hundred alleles exist, but about nine account for over ninety five percent of phenotypes. They fall into three groups. Star one and star two are fully functional. Star three, four, five and six are nonfunctional. Star ten, seventeen and forty one have reduced function.

For a drug that C Y P two D six clears, a poor metabolizer accumulates it and has adverse effects at standard doses. For a prodrug it activates, a poor metabolizer makes too little active drug, and the therapy fails. Codeine is that kind of prodrug. She said, Codeine is metabolized by two D six to morphine. An ultrarapid metabolizer quickly turns a normal dose into a large amount of morphine, which can suppress breathing. Children died after codeine for cough, so codeine cough syrup is no longer given to kids. A super dose would only fit a drug that C Y P two D six clears, never codeine.
